note: The £1,000 trading and property allowances, from HMRC's guidance. Income Tax uses the UK tax file; Class 4 National Insurance on trading profits uses the self-employed tax file (data/tax/gb/gb-se).

both.quote: You can get up to £1,000 each tax year in tax-free allowances for property or trading income from 6 April 2017. If you have both types of income, you’ll get a £1,000 allowance for each.

partial.quote: If you use the allowances you can deduct up to £1,000, but not more than the amount of your income. This is known as ‘partial relief’.

expenses.quote: If your expenses are more than your income it may be beneficial to claim expenses instead of the allowances.

trading.quote: The trading allowance is a tax exemption of up to £1,000 a year for individuals with trading income from: self-employment casual services, for example, babysitting or gardening (helpsheet 325 has more information about other taxable income) hiring personal equipment, for example, power tools

tellTrading.quote: You must tell HMRC if you have: gross trading income over £1,000 — register for Self Assessment other gross income over £1,000 up to £2,500 — contact HMRC other income over £2,500 — register for Self Assessment

property.quote: The property allowance is a tax exemption of up to £1,000 a year for individuals with income from land or property. If you own a property jointly with others, you’re each eligible for the £1,000 allowance against your share of the gross rental income.

tellProperty.quote: You must tell HMRC if you have: gross property income over £1,000 up to £2,500 — contact HMRC property income over £2,500 — register for Self Assessment

noRentARoom.quote: You cannot use this allowance on income from letting a room in your own home under the Rent a Room Scheme.

cannot.quote: You cannot use the allowances in a tax year, if you have any trade or property income from: a company you or someone connected to you owns or controls a partnership where you or someone connected to you are partners your employer or the employer of your spouse or civil partner

register.quote: If your gross income for a tax year is more than £1,000, you must register for Self Assessment by 5 October in the following tax year.

noOther.quote: You cannot deduct any other expenses or allowances if you claim the allowances.

sources.title: Tax-free allowances on property and trading income
